# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring from the same side as FIG. 1 is viewed, so that the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. The form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, and the segment on which the ring drive face 36 lies and its position on the outer boundary, are shown schematically.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by inner and outer circular boundaries, is the segmented cam ring 20. The region within the inner boundary is open.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments. The upper segment is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower segment is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26.

At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus and open at the face toward the viewer, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints; those positions are shown schematically. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the width of the annulus and inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary; that handedness is shown schematically.

The ring drive face 36 lies on the outer boundary of the lower segment, the second cam ring segment 24, just below the right joint: there the outer boundary runs for a short length as a straight surface slanting inward toward that joint. The outer boundary of the upper segment, the first cam ring segment 22, is circular throughout.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment, in its upper left.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment, at the bottom.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the surfaces meeting at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface near the right joint.

input.summary: Applied both reviewer fixes, confined to two figure briefs. FIG. 2 now designates the segment on which the ring drive face 36 lies, and its position on the outer boundary, as items shown schematically, while the face itself stays on the second cam ring segment 24 so FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 continue to agree. FIG. 4 now designates the width of the gap between the two frame bodies at the latch joint as schematic, matching how FIG. 6 already treats that same clearance. Both briefs crossed the 2800-character ceiling once the designations went in, so I removed three redundant clauses that the designations or the surrounding text already cover; all six briefs are under the limit. No claim, description, drawing-description, or numeral-table text changed, and every per-sheet numeral list is unchanged.
reasoning: The drive-face designation went into FIG. 2's opening schematic list rather than into the body, so the geometry that keeps the sheet correct stays positive and specific: the face is still a short straight slanting surface on the outer boundary of the lower segment just below the right joint, and the first cam ring segment's outer boundary is still stated to be circular throughout. That second statement is what stopped the renderer from putting the flat on the wrong segment two rounds ago, so I kept it and let the new designation carry the message that the assignment is a drawing choice.

The face stays on segment 24 because FIG. 4, viewed from the opposite side, shows it on the band that maps to segment 24, and the review confirmed the wedge's inward advance drives that segment in the sense the FIG. 2 slot handedness needs. Moving it would have broken a cross-figure relationship that currently checks out.

FIG. 4's gap designation was worded to cover the same feature FIG. 6 already designates, so the two briefs now treat the latch-joint clearance identically. The body of FIG. 4 still states positively that a narrow gap separates the two bodies and that the band ends meet in contact within it, which is the relationship the sheet has to show.

To make room, I dropped 'The length of the slanting surface is shown schematically' from FIG. 2, since the new list item already designates the face's position on the outer boundary; shortened the note about the ring being shown removed from the frame, which the brief's opening sentence already says; and in FIG. 4 folded the handle silhouette designation into the handle list item as 'its plain outline and constant width' and dropped one repetition of the housing numeral where the walls had just been named. Nothing structural was removed from either brief.

The specification remains neutral on both points, describing only that the ring drive face is presented at a position the wedge can reach and saying nothing about a clearance at the latch joint, so neither fix touched draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md.

# FIG. 1

Plan view of the assembled split pipe clamp, closed around a pipe, viewed along the pipe axis. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

A circle at the centre of the drawing area is the pipe 90, seen end on.

An annular frame body of substantial width surrounds the pipe 90, bounded by an inner circle spaced outward from it and an outer circle.

Two radial joint lines, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annular frame body into two semicircular bodies: the upper is the first frame half 10 and the lower is the second frame half 12.

At the left joint is the hinge 14, drawn schematically as a small circle on that joint line with a short knuckle block reaching to it from each frame end.

At the right joint is the latch 16, drawn schematically as a rectangular block lying outside the annular frame body and bridging both frame ends, with an elongated lever extending away from the frame. The latch 16 is drawn in its over-center position, in which the pipe 90 is clamped; the lever attitude there is shown schematically.

Three jaw carriages 30 are spaced around the annular frame body, one at the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right. Each crosses the inner boundary of that body and reaches radially inward toward the pipe 90. The topmost lies on the first frame half 10 and the other two on the second frame half 12; these positions are shown schematically.

Each jaw carriage 30 carries at its inner end a separate member, the jaw pad 40, joined to it at a small circle, a pivot shown schematically; its inner face is a concave arc meeting the outer surface of the pipe 90.

A short broken cutting-plane line lies wholly in the upper part of the view, on the radial centre line of the topmost jaw carriage 30. Its upper end is a short distance above the outer boundary of the annular frame body and its lower end is at the concave face of the jaw pad 40 of that carriage, where that face meets the pipe 90, so the line stops at the pipe 90. A short arrow at each end points to the same side of the line. That line is the cutting plane of FIG. 3, the arrows giving the direction in which that section is viewed.

# FIG. 2

Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring from the same side as FIG. 1 is viewed, so that the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. The form of the meeting surfaces at the two joints, and the segment on which the ring drive face 36 lies and its position on the outer boundary, are shown schematically.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by inner and outer circular boundaries, is the segmented cam ring 20. The region within the inner boundary is open.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments. The upper segment is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower segment is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet along complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26.

At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings are formed in the annulus and open at the face toward the viewer, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints; those positions are shown schematically. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening lying within the width of the annulus and inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary; that handedness is shown schematically.

The ring drive face 36 lies on the outer boundary of the lower segment, the second cam ring segment 24, just below the right joint: there the outer boundary runs for a short length as a straight surface slanting inward toward that joint. The outer boundary of the upper segment, the first cam ring segment 22, is circular throughout.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment, in its upper left.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment, at the bottom.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the surfaces meeting at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface near the right joint.

# FIG. 3

Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the carriage return spring 44, the direction in which the annular guide 18 opens, and the way the oblique slot 34 is formed in the segmented cam ring 20.

A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view, with a groove in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, the two meeting.

The groove is bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left; its proportions are shown schematically. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. A narrow rectangular opening runs into the block from its left face and closes within the block toward the right. That opening is the oblique slot 34. It lies in the lower portion of the block, leaving a broad hatched region of the block above it and hatched material below it and right of its closed end. Its depth is shown schematically.

The channel runs downward from the mouth of the groove and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the mouth of the groove and into the opening in the block lying in the groove, its upper and lower sides facing the sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A compression spring drawn as a zigzag line acts between the jaw carriage 30 and the frame body, urging the jaw carriage 30 upward, that is, radially outward. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body hangs from the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 on a small circle, a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 18 annular guide: target the groove wall above the block lying in it.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the block in the groove, above the opening.
- 30 jaw carriage: target the hatching of the block in the channel.
- 32 follower: target well inside the post.
- 34 oblique slot: target the open space of the opening, right of the post.
- 38 radial guide: target the right wall of the channel, below the groove mouth.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the lowest body.
- 44 carriage return spring: target the zigzag line.

# FIG. 4

Enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end of the clamp, closed, parts shown in section, viewed along the axis of the frame from the side opposite that from which FIG. 1 is viewed. Radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the housing and cavity, the frame-wall interruption, the width of the gap between the two frame bodies, the pivot mounting of the latch handle 50 and the opening through which it passes, its plain outline and constant width, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 drawn as one spring symbol.

At the lower left a hatched body in section holds a hatched arcuate band from the left; at the lower right a second holds a like band from the right. A narrow gap separates the two bodies, and in it the band ends meet along complementary surfaces in contact. Both bands are the segmented cam ring 20.

The frame wall radially outside the left band is interrupted, exposing its upper side; near the right end that side runs as a short straight surface slanting down to the right, the ring drive face 36.

Above the gap a hatched enclosure, the latch housing 58, reaches across both bodies, its left, right and top walls enclosing a cavity opening downward over the ring drive face 36.

A block, the wedge 52, lies in the cavity between those walls; its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears on it, so downward movement drives the band left.

Above it the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag line rising from the wedge 52 into the cavity.

The latch handle 50 is a plain elongated lever of constant width, its two long straight parallel edges running unbroken from the pivot to the free tip, where a short straight end closes it, the area between those edges plain. It is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle at the cavity's upper right, and a short arm reaches from that pivot down and left onto the upper end of that stack. The top and right walls stop short of one another, leaving an opening through which the lever runs up and right, leaning right past upright, the over-center position.

A slender pin, the indicator pin 56, rises from that stack through a hole in the top wall.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the left band.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the left band.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the lever.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line.
- 56 indicator pin: target the pin above the top wall.

# FIG. 4

Enlarged fragmentary view of the latch end, closed, parts shown in section, viewed along the frame axis from the side opposite that from which FIG. 1 is viewed. Radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the form of the housing and cavity, the attitude of the latch handle 50 in the over-center position, the frame-wall interruption, the length of the ring drive face 36, the width of the gap between the two frame bodies, the pivot mounting of the latch handle 50 and the opening through which it passes, the plain outline and constant width of that handle, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 drawn as one spring symbol.

At the lower left a hatched body in section holds a hatched arcuate band from the left; at the lower right a second holds a like band from the right. A narrow gap separates the two bodies, and in it the band ends meet along complementary surfaces in contact. Both bands are the segmented cam ring 20.

The frame wall radially outside the left band is interrupted, exposing its upper side; near the right end that side runs as a short straight surface slanting down to the right, the ring drive face 36.

Above the gap a hatched enclosure, the latch housing 58, reaches across both bodies, its left, right and top walls enclosing a cavity opening downward over the ring drive face 36.

A block, the wedge 52, lies in the cavity between those walls; its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears on it, so downward movement drives the band left.

Above it the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag line rising from the wedge 52 into the cavity.

The latch handle 50 is a plain elongated lever of constant width, its two long straight parallel edges running unbroken from the pivot to the free tip, where a short straight end closes it, the area between those edges plain. It is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle at the cavity's upper right, and a short arm reaches from that pivot down and left onto the upper end of that stack. The top and right walls stop short of one another, leaving an opening through which the lever runs up and right, leaning right past upright, the over-center position.

A slender pin, the indicator pin 56, rises from that stack through a hole in the top wall.

# FIG. 3

Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis, the left of this view being the axial side from which FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 are viewed. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the carriage return spring 44, the direction in which the annular guide 18 opens, and the way the oblique slot 34 is formed in the segmented cam ring 20.

A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view, with a groove in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, the two meeting.

The groove is bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left; its proportions are shown schematically. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. A narrow rectangular opening runs into the block from its left face and closes within it toward the right. That opening is the oblique slot 34. It lies in the lower portion of the block, leaving a broad hatched region above it and hatched material below it and right of its closed end. Its depth is shown schematically.

The channel runs downward from the mouth of the groove and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the mouth of the groove and into the opening in the block in the groove, its upper and lower sides facing the sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A compression spring drawn as a zigzag line acts between the jaw carriage 30 and the frame body, urging that carriage upward, that is, radially outward. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body hangs from the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 on a small circle, a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 18 annular guide: target the groove wall above the block lying in it.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the block in the groove, above the opening.
- 30 jaw carriage: target the hatching of the block in the channel.
- 32 follower: target well inside the post.
- 34 oblique slot: target the open space of the opening, right of the post.
- 38 radial guide: target the right wall of the channel, below the groove mouth.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the lowest body.
- 44 carriage return spring: target the zigzag line.

# FIG. 1

Plan view of the assembled split pipe clamp, closed around a pipe, viewed along the pipe axis. Black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

A circle at the centre of the drawing area is the pipe 90, seen end on.

An annular frame body of substantial width surrounds the pipe 90, bounded by an inner circle spaced outward from it and an outer circle.

Two radial joint lines, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annular frame body into two semicircular bodies: the upper is the first frame half 10 and the lower is the second frame half 12.

At the left joint is the hinge 14, drawn schematically as a small circle on that joint line with a short knuckle block reaching to it from each frame end.

At the right joint is the latch 16, drawn schematically as a rectangular block lying outside the frame body and bridging both frame ends, with an elongated lever extending away from the frame. The latch 16 is drawn in its over-center position, in which the pipe 90 is clamped; the lever attitude there is shown schematically.

Three jaw carriages 30 are spaced around the annular frame body, one at the top, one at the lower left, one at the lower right, each crossing the inner boundary of that body and reaching radially inward toward the pipe 90. The topmost lies on the first frame half 10 and the other two on the second frame half 12; these positions are shown schematically.

Each jaw carriage 30 carries at its inner end a separate member, the jaw pad 40, joined to it at a small circle, a pivot shown schematically; its inner face is a concave arc meeting the pipe 90.

A short broken cutting-plane line lies wholly in the upper part of the view, on the radial centre line of the topmost jaw carriage 30. Its upper end is a short distance above the outer boundary of that body and its lower end is at the concave face of the jaw pad 40 of that carriage, where that face meets the pipe 90, so the line stops at the pipe 90. A short arrow at each end points horizontally to the left of the view, both arrows to the same side of the line. That line is the cutting plane of FIG. 3, the arrows giving the direction in which that section is viewed.

10	
11	The channel runs downward from the groove mouth and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38.

That post is the follower 32.

# FIG. 3

Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis, the view's left being the axial side from which FIG. 1 and FIG. 2 are viewed. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. Shown schematically: the carriage return spring 44, the direction in which the annular guide 18 opens, and the way the oblique slot 34 is formed in the segmented cam ring 20.

A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view, with a groove in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, the two meeting.

The groove is bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left; its proportions are shown schematically. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. A narrow rectangular opening runs into the block from its left face and closes within it toward the right. That opening is the oblique slot 34. It lies in the lower portion of the block, leaving a broad hatched region above it and hatched material below it and right of its closed end. Its depth is shown schematically.

The channel runs downward from the groove mouth and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the groove mouth and into the opening in the block in the groove, its upper and lower sides facing the sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A compression spring drawn as a zigzag line acts between the jaw carriage 30 and the frame body, urging that carriage upward, that is, radially outward. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body hangs from the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 on a small circle, a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc.

- 34 oblique slot: target the open space of the opening, right of the post.
- 38 radial guide: target the right wall of the channel, below the groove mouth.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the lowest body.
- 44 carriage return spring: target the zigzag line.

reasoning: The drive-face length is designated in both places it is drawn, FIG. 2 and FIG. 4, rather than in one.
